01.h1: How to fall asleep more easily with MeditaDream
01.accroche: How to fall asleep more peacefully: slow down your thoughts and let your body go.
pitch: Wondering how to fall asleep when your mind won’t slow down? MeditaDream gives you a free sleep meditation made for bed, lights off. Drifting into Sleep is guided relaxation for sleep. It takes you down gently and never wakes you at the end, so you can drift off before it finishes. On longer nights, Sleep Journey stays with you for 27 minutes, without any pressure to fall asleep.

Rather hear no words at all? Pick sleep sounds such as waves, forest or a mountain stream, set the timer from 5 to 60 minutes, and the sound fades out on its own. Choose your voice, slow it to 0.75×, then download everything once. This mindfulness sleep app then keeps playing in airplane mode, with no network to disturb you.

Learning how to sleep better starts earlier in the evening, too. Precise Gratitude ends the day on something you enjoyed. Your Instant Refuge uses guided imagery for sleep: a reassuring place to rest your mind. The Oracle suggests three meditations for how you feel tonight. You can even write your own bedtime session and hear your phone read it aloud.
etapes: Half an hour before bed, open the Oracle and type how you feel, like “tired but wired” or “anxious and awake.” It suggests three free guided meditations for sleep and anxiety, or you can pick a short session like Precise Gratitude.
Lights off, start Drifting into Sleep or Sleep Journey. Both are made to be heard in bed and end with no wake-up, so you can stop listening whenever sleep comes.
On nights when words feel like too much, open Ambient sounds, choose waves or a mountain stream, and set the timer from 5 to 60 minutes. The sound fades out gently.
Download your favorite sessions once, choose your voice and a slower pace, then switch to airplane mode. In the morning, note any dream that stayed with you in your Dream Journal.
faq: How do I use MeditaDream to fall asleep?

Get into bed, turn off the lights and start a free guided sleep meditation: Drifting into Sleep (16 minutes) or Sleep Journey (27 minutes). Don’t try to follow every word: if you fall asleep, the session simply ends without waking you. On nights when you’d rather hear no voice, play sleep sounds on the timer and let them fade out.
Should I choose a sleep meditation or sleep sounds?

Both have their place. A guided sleep meditation gives a busy mind something gentle to follow, like the weight of your body or the rhythm of your breath. Sleep sounds suit nights when words feel like too much. You can start with a voice, then switch to waves or a forest stream once you feel ready.
What if my mind keeps racing during a sleep meditation?

That’s normal, and it isn’t a failure. Each time you notice a thought, gently come back to what the voice describes, like the weight of your head on the pillow. Short practices help too: Your Instant Refuge or A Happy Memory Through Three Senses give your mind a pleasant place to rest before the lights go out.

programme.titre: A Relaxing Bedtime Routine to Help You Fall Asleep Faster
programme.intro: Over three weeks, you build a night routine for better sleep, one small step at a time. It’s for anyone who lies awake with a busy mind, even if you’ve never meditated. You start with wind-downs of three or four minutes, learn to release your body and quiet your thoughts, then end with sleep meditations that don’t wake you. Plan 3 to 30 minutes each night.

etapes.titre: Give your evening a clear ending
etapes.texte: A routine works through repetition, so begin with a simple cue that tells your body the day is over. Choose the voice and pace you like best, then play Precise Gratitude or Your Instant Refuge each evening. One ends your day on something you enjoyed, the other in a reassuring place. Short is fine: the cue is what counts.
etapes.geste: Every evening at the same time, dim the lights, sit on your bed and play one short session before lying down.
etapes.repere: You’re ready when this little ritual feels natural and your evenings start to have a calm, clear ending.

etapes.titre: Release the tension of the day
etapes.texte: Now your routine moves into bed. Lights off, lying down, let Body Scan — Mapping the Body from Within guide your attention region by region. On the other nights, Breathing with the Whole Body lets each breath spread far beyond your lungs. You’re not trying to fall asleep yet. You’re learning to find tension, in the jaw, shoulders or belly, and let some of it go.
etapes.geste: In bed, lights off, alternate the two sessions night after night, with the sessions downloaded and your phone in airplane mode.
etapes.repere: You’re ready when you can spot a tight area in your body and soften it a little on your own.

etapes.titre: Quiet a racing mind
etapes.texte: Some nights your body is ready, but your mind keeps going. This stage gives your thoughts something gentle to follow. Hearing — the Distant Singing Bowl rests your attention on a single sound, and The Body Under a Waterfall turns letting go into a soothing image of water. If a worry won’t leave, write it down first: once it’s on paper, it can wait until morning.
etapes.geste: Before lights out, write one line in your Emotional Journal about what’s on your mind, then play one of this stage’s sessions.
etapes.repere: You’re ready when a passing thought no longer carries you away, and coming back to the sound or the water feels easy.

etapes.titre: Let sleep come on its own
etapes.texte: Now put the pieces together: your short cue, a line in your journal, then a sleep meditation made for bed. Drifting into Sleep and Sleep Journey end with no wake-up, so there’s nothing to finish and no goal to reach. When you’d rather hear no voice, let sleep sounds fade out on the timer instead.
etapes.geste: Keep the same bedtime all week, weekends included: your cue first, then lights off and one sleep meditation or sleep sounds.
etapes.repere: The routine is yours when it runs almost on its own, and some nights you no longer hear the end of the session.

programme.apres: Keep the steps that work for you as your sleep routine, and repeat the full 21 days after a hectic week. On calm evenings, visit The Dream Forest.

When Everything Moves Too Fast grounds you through your eyes, your feet and your breath, Relax Very Quickly loosens your body in three minutes, and Calming Down After an Argument helps the tension ease after a conflict.

When you have more time, deep breathing exercises for stress take you further. Breathing with the Whole Body and The Luminous Breath offer gentle breathwork that calms your attention. faq: How do I use MeditaDream for stress relief?

Start small. When stress rises, play a session from the 4 Minutes category, such as When Everything Moves Too Fast. Then build a habit of meditation for stress management. Choose one longer breathing session a day, like The Luminous Breath, at a time set with the meditation alarm. If you’re unsure what fits, the Oracle suggests three meditations based on what you type.
What is box breathing, and can I practice it here?

Box breathing is a breathing exercise in four equal counts: breathe in for four, hold for four, breathe out for four, hold for four, as if tracing a square. The Learning library explains it step by step, and you can practice it on your own over an ambient sound on the timer. If holding your breath feels uncomfortable, simply skip the holds.
How long should a meditation for stress relief last?

There’s no magic number. Three or four minutes can already help you step out of the rush, which is why the 4 Minutes sessions exist. Regularity matters more than length: a short daily session is easier to keep up than one long session a week. When you have more time, try a session of 13 to 25 minutes.

programme.intro: This daily meditation plan is for busy people who feel stress building up through the day. Over four weeks, you move from 4-minute breaks to breathing exercises and slow qigong, one habit at a time. Plan 3 to 30 minutes a day. Short sessions count: coming back every day matters more than sitting for a long time.

etapes.titre: Take a 4-minute break every day
etapes.texte: Start with the smallest habit that can work. Pick the moment your day usually speeds up and give it a few minutes. When Everything Moves Too Fast brings you back to one object, the ground and your breath, and Relax Very Quickly releases your body from forehead to feet. This week isn’t about deep calm. It’s about remembering to stop.

etapes.repere: You’re ready when you take your break even without the reminder, or notice stress rising before it peaks.

etapes.titre: Train your attention to come back
etapes.texte: A stressed mind races ahead to what might go wrong. This week, add one longer session each morning and keep your 4-minute break. Stabilizing Attention on the Breath — Ariadne’s Thread teaches you to come back each time you drift, and Observing Thoughts — Watching the Trains Go by helps you let worries pass instead of chasing them.
etapes.geste: Each morning, before you check your phone, sit in the same chair for one 13- or 15-minute session.
etapes.repere: You’re ready when you notice your mind spinning and can return to the breath without getting annoyed with yourself.

etapes.titre: Breathe your way back to calm
etapes.texte: With steadier attention, breathing exercises can take you deeper. Breathing with the Whole Body lets each breath spread like rings on water, and The Luminous Breath pairs every in-breath with a gentle light flowing down to your legs. etapes.repere: You’re ready when a few slow breaths are enough to loosen your shoulders, even in the middle of a busy day.

On days you’re unsure what you need, tell the Oracle how you feel and try one of its three suggestions.
etapes.geste: Three evenings this week, clear a little space at home and follow one qigong session standing, in comfortable clothes.
etapes.repere: You know what to reach for: a short break at work, a breathing session at home, slow movement when your body feels tight.

03.seo: How to Calm Anxiety: Free Meditations for Worry and Fear
03.desc: Learn how to calm anxiety with 4-minute anchors, relaxation for anxiety and gentle meditations on fear and worry. Free, no subscription, no ads.
03.h1: How to calm anxiety with MeditaDream, at your own pace
03.accroche: Learn how to calm anxiety gently: meet worry, fear and self-criticism with kinder eyes. Support for your well-being, never a replacement for care.
pitch: When worry takes over, you don’t need a lecture. You need something to hold on to. MeditaDream’s free guided meditation for anxiety starts small: Your Instant Refuge brings a reassuring place to mind in four minutes, After Receiving Bad News pulls you back from worst-case scenarios, and When You Feel Watched or Judged separates facts from guesses about others.

Then you can look at fear itself, gently. Releasing Fear explores what your fear is trying to protect, while Fear of Failure and Fear of Judgment each take one worry at a time. Observing Thoughts — Watching the Trains Go by is a guided meditation for anxiety and overthinking. This simple anxiety mindfulness practice teaches you to let anxious thoughts pass instead of feeding them.

On low days, Daily Gratitude and When You Feel Like Giving Up offer a small step forward. Tell the Oracle how you feel to get three suggestions, or search “fear” to find the right session. Unlike many meditation apps for anxiety, there’s no account and no subscription. Your Emotional Journal keeps track of the journey privately, on your phone.
etapes: In the moment, open the Oracle and type what you feel, such as “knot in my stomach before work.” It suggests three meditations; a 4-minute one like Your Instant Refuge is a good first step.
When worries loop, play Observing Thoughts — Watching the Trains Go by. You practice noticing a thought, then letting it pass, like a train you don’t have to board.
Once a week, choose one fear and meet it calmly: Fear of Failure, Fear of Judgment or Releasing Fear. Slow the voice to 0.75× if a gentler pace feels better.
After each session, write a few words in your history or your Emotional Journal. Over the weeks, you’ll see which sessions help you most, privately, on your phone.
faq: How do I use MeditaDream to calm anxiety?

Use it in two ways. In the moment, a short session such as Your Instant Refuge or After Receiving Bad News helps you come back to the present. Later, a meditation to reduce anxiety, like Releasing Fear or Welcoming a Difficult Emotion, changes how you relate to worry. And when you don’t know where to start, the Oracle picks three meditations for how you feel.
What if meditating makes me more anxious?

It can happen, especially with eyes closed or long silences. Keep your eyes open and choose short exercises to help with anxiety, like the 4 Minutes sessions. Stop whenever you need to: nothing is forced. Anchoring in something concrete, like your feet on the floor or a sound in the room, often feels easier than following the breath. These anchors are also what many people try when they wonder how to calm a panic attack. If panic comes back often, talk to a health professional.
Can MeditaDream replace professional support?

No. MeditaDream offers moments of calm and reflection for your well-being, but it does not replace a health professional. If anxiety or low moods last, feel overwhelming or get in the way of daily life, please talk to a health professional. If you ever feel in danger, contact emergency services right away. Meditation can sit alongside that support.

What is a body scan, and is it good for beginners?

A body scan means moving your attention slowly through your body, from one area to the next, simply noticing what you feel: warmth, tension or nothing at all. MeditaDream is a well-being app and does not replace a health professional. faq: How do I use MeditaDream to manage my emotions?

Combine three things: a session in the moment, a regular practice and a journal. Calming Down After an Argument helps when emotions run high. What is self-compassion?

Self-compassion means treating yourself the way you’d treat a good friend who’s struggling: with patience instead of harsh criticism. It isn’t self-pity, and it doesn’t mean ignoring your mistakes. What is the third eye, and how do I start?

In yogic tradition, the third eye, or Ajna, is the sixth chakra, pictured between the eyebrows and linked to intuition and inner vision. Start with The Third Eye and the Two Physical Eyes, and don’t force anything: images may come, or they may not.
Do I need to believe in anything to use these meditations?

No. You can treat chakras, guides or your higher self as traditions, symbols or images for your imagination, and still enjoy the sessions as inner experiences. MeditaDream has no dogma and asks for no belief, only curiosity and a quiet moment. Take what speaks to you and leave the rest.

What’s the difference between zen meditation, vipassana and qigong?

Zen meditation, rooted in Chan and Japanese Buddhism, centers on sitting and simply being present. Do I need to be Buddhist to practice?

programme.apres: Lucidity often takes time, so keep your Dream Journal going and repeat Weeks 2 to 4. On tired nights, choose rest over exploration.

13.seo: Letting Go, Forgiveness and Grief: A Gentle Meditation App
13.desc: Meditations for letting go, forgiveness and grief: say what was left unsaid, honor a pet who’s gone, forgive at your own pace. No subscription, no ads.
13.h1: Letting go, forgiving and grieving, at your own pace
13.accroche: Letting go, gently: a personal space for reflection in times of loss or change.
pitch: Grief has no timetable, and no grief meditation can rush it. What MeditaDream offers is a quiet space to be with what you feel. The Garden of Reunion invites you to explore words left unsaid, My Departed Animal honors the memory of a pet who’s gone, and Welcoming a Difficult Emotion makes room for sadness and anger.

Forgiveness comes at its own pace, and it’s never an obligation. Each forgiveness meditation here respects that. Forgiving Without Forgetting looks at resentment without forcing you to forgive. Forgiving Yourself works gently with guilt, toward a more forgiving self-talk. Heart-Centered Ho’oponopono draws on ho’oponopono, meaning “to make right” in Hawaiian. As a letting go meditation, The Forest of Thorns explores how you face what stands in your way.

Some days call for a refuge. Create your own sanctuary, or try a few lines of journaling: grief can ease when it finds words. Let the Oracle suggest three meditations for how you feel today. There’s no account, and everything stays private on your phone.
etapes: Begin softly: tell the Oracle what you’re going through, like “I miss my father,” and choose one of its three suggestions, or start with the seven-minute Compassion Meditation.
When you feel ready, play The Garden of Reunion or My Departed Animal. Choose a quiet moment, keep tissues nearby, and know you can pause at any time.
Approach forgiveness step by step: Forgiving Without Forgetting first, then Forgiving Yourself or Heart-Centered Ho’oponopono, at your own pace and only if you wish.

Create a personal sanctuary, a safe inner place to return to, and write in your journals after each session. Simple grief journal prompts help: What do I miss most? What would I like to say? Everything stays private, on your phone.
faq: How do I use MeditaDream when I’m grieving?

Go at your own pace. Short, gentle sessions like Compassion Meditation can keep you company on hard days. When you feel ready, The Garden of Reunion and My Departed Animal offer a space to remember and say what was left unsaid. Writing in your journals afterward can help too, and the Oracle can suggest three meditations for today.
Do I have to forgive in order to let go?

No. Letting go doesn’t require forgiving, and forgiving doesn’t mean forgetting or excusing what happened. Forgiving Without Forgetting explores resentment without imposing forgiveness, and The Forest of Thorns looks at how you face what hurts. Some people find forgiveness along the way; others simply find more peace. Both are valid.
Can MeditaDream replace support during grief?

No. MeditaDream offers a personal space for reflection, but it does not replace a health professional or the people close to you. If your grief feels overwhelming, lasts a long time or makes daily life hard, please reach out to a health professional or a support group. Meditation can sit alongside that help, never instead of it.

programme.titre: A Gentle Meditation Routine for Grief, Forgiveness and Letting Go
programme.intro: Grief, forgiveness and letting go keep no schedule, so this path has no countdown. It offers a quiet space for anyone living through a loss, a breakup or a change they didn’t choose. Each stage waits for you as long as you need. Sessions last 7 to 25 minutes, on the days you choose, and you can pause or stop at any moment.
programme.rythme: 7 to 25 min, when you feel ready

etapes.titre: A gentle place to begin
etapes.texte: When you’re grieving, even sitting still can feel hard, so start small. Compassion Meditation offers seven minutes of warmth, first toward yourself. Welcoming a Difficult Emotion lets sadness or anger be there, without asking them to leave. You can also shape a personal sanctuary in the app, a place with its own name and atmosphere where each session can begin.
etapes.geste: When you feel able, sit somewhere comfortable with a blanket or a warm drink and play one session; seven minutes is enough.
etapes.repere: You may feel ready to go on when you can stay with what you feel for a few minutes, even through tears.

etapes.titre: Make room for memories
etapes.texte: Memories can hurt and comfort at the same time. The Attic of Forgotten Objects leaves you free to open each room, or to keep it closed. The Garden of Reunion invites you to say the words left unsaid, and My Departed Animal reconnects you with a pet who has passed. If words come afterward, your journals can hold them, privately on your phone.
etapes.geste: Choose a time when no one will need you for an hour, play one session, then sit by a window for a while.
etapes.repere: You may be ready for the next stage when remembering brings some warmth along with the pain.

etapes.titre: Explore forgiveness, without pressure
etapes.texte: Forgiveness can’t be forced, and it never means excusing what happened. Forgiving Without Forgetting explores what it might mean for you, then lets you decide: set it down, or keep it. Forgiving Yourself works gently with guilt, the “if only” thoughts that so often follow a loss. A slower voice and pace can make both sessions feel gentler.
etapes.geste: Try these sessions only on a day you feel steady, and stop whenever it feels like too much.
etapes.repere: You may be ready to go on when a memory brings less blame, toward someone else or toward yourself.

etapes.titre: Let go, little by little
etapes.texte: Letting go isn’t forgetting. It’s finding a way to carry what happened with a little more ease. Heart-Centered Ho’oponopono repeats four simple phrases with the rhythm of the breath. The Forest of Thorns has you stop fighting what snags you, and Gratitude to Your Guides gives thanks to the people who mattered. On uncertain days, the Oracle can suggest three meditations.
etapes.geste: When it feels right, play one session a week, and return to any earlier stage whenever you need to.
etapes.repere: You notice moments of peace, or even gratitude, alongside the sadness, and you know where to turn on hard days.

programme.apres: Return to any stage whenever you need it. If grief feels too heavy or lasts a long time, please reach out to a health professional or a support group.

14.seo: Escape Into 17 Immersive Worlds: A Free App With No Ads
14.desc: Escape into 17 immersive worlds of guided visualization, from Atlantis to a cosmic temple, plus time-travel adventures. No subscription, no ads.
14.h1: How MeditaDream helps you escape into immersive worlds
14.accroche: Change worlds through meditation, picture new places and slow down into contemplation.
pitch: Sometimes the best rest is somewhere else. MeditaDream, an immersive meditation app, takes you there in minutes: ride a golden seahorse through Underwater Atlantis, climb to The Ancient Temple through the mountain mist, or rest above the clouds on The Floating Island. Seventeen worlds await, each a guided visualization with its own scenery and pace.

Prefer a story? The Mini Adventures are time travel for the mind: Versailles — a Day in 1700, Japan — on the Road to Kyoto in 1600 and The Unknown Planet. The Train of Memories even takes you through the stages of a life. Add an ambient sound, choose your voice, and let the scenery do the rest.

Your journeys leave traces. Create personal sanctuaries with their own setting and ambience, keep the symbolic objects you bring back, and watch your dragon companion and its island grow with your practice. Every guided visualization, free and without ads, downloads once and plays anywhere, even offline.
etapes: Open Meditation Worlds and pick the setting that calls you today: Underwater Atlantis, The Infinite Crystal Cave, Journey Through the Galaxy or any of the 17 worlds.
Settle comfortably, put on headphones and add an ambient sound if you like. Each world lasts 13 to 19 minutes, a true break in your day.
For a longer escape, choose a Mini Adventure such as Versailles — a Day in 1700 (30 minutes) or Japan — on the Road to Kyoto in 1600 (34 minutes).
Afterward, save the objects you found in your collection, build a sanctuary inspired by your favorite world, and download your worlds for trips with no signal.
faq: How do I use MeditaDream for immersive journeys?

Choose a world or a Mini Adventure to match your mood: water and calm with Underwater Atlantis, height and space with The Floating Island, history with Versailles — a Day in 1700. Put on headphones, dim the lights and let the voice guide you. Afterward, keep the objects you found in your collection or build your own sanctuary.
What is a guided visualization?

A guided visualization is a meditation where a voice describes a place or a scene, and you picture it with all your senses: what you see, hear and feel. It’s a gentle way to relax and spark your imagination. Don’t worry if the images stay blurry: sensing the atmosphere is enough, and it often gets easier with practice.
Can I take these journeys without an internet connection?

Yes. Download a world or a Mini Adventure once, and it plays offline: on a plane, on a train or in a cabin with no signal. MeditaDream is also free, with no ads to break the spell and no account to create, so nothing pulls you out of your journey.

programme.titre: Escape Into Immersive Worlds: 14 Days of Daily Guided Meditation
programme.intro: Two weeks to travel without leaving home. This daily guided meditation path is for anyone who needs a real break: each day, one guided visualization, from 13-minute worlds to a 34-minute walk to old Kyoto. Plan 13 to 34 minutes a day, ideally with headphones. Download your journeys once, and they play anywhere, even offline.

etapes.titre: Take short escapes
etapes.texte: Start with short trips. On days one to three, visit one short world a day, such as The Desert Oasis or The Cosmic Temple, about 13 minutes each. On day four, The Unknown Planet sends you exploring, letting each question change the way you look. No effort needed: let the scenery come to you.
etapes.geste: Pick a fixed escape time, like your lunch break or the end of the workday, and keep it for the whole two weeks.
etapes.repere: You’re ready when you can sense a world’s colors and sounds without straining, even if the images stay soft.

etapes.titre: Travel with all your senses
etapes.texte: Now stay a little longer and use every sense. Choose worlds of water and sky, like Underwater Atlantis or The Floating Island, and add an ambient sound that matches the scene. On day eight, The Train of Memories turns the journey inward: station after station, you watch the habits, tastes and decisions that made a life.
etapes.geste: Before each journey, close your eyes for three slow breaths and choose one sense to follow closely: sight, sound or touch.
etapes.repere: You’re ready when you come back from a world with one vivid detail you could describe to a friend.

etapes.titre: Travel back in time
etapes.texte: Time for a longer escape. Versailles — a Day in 1700 takes you to the royal court for a whole day: the bows, the glances, a world revolving around one man. On the days before and after, revisit the world you liked most so far. Download the adventure first, so a weak signal never breaks the spell.
etapes.geste: Set aside a 30-minute window with nothing planned after it, sit or lie back comfortably, and let the story run to the end.
etapes.repere: You’re ready when half an hour passes easily and you feel you’ve truly been somewhere else.

etapes.titre: Take the long road and make a world your own
etapes.texte: Your final journey is the longest: Japan — on the Road to Kyoto in 1600, a walk with your senses awake, never knowing what waits around the next bend. To close the two weeks, gather the details you loved most, a color, a sound, a light, into a personal sanctuary with its own name and atmosphere. Your dragon’s island has grown with your practice.
etapes.geste: Over the last three days, play the journey once; on the other two, revisit a favorite world, then shape your sanctuary from its details.
etapes.repere: You have a favorite world, a sanctuary of your own, and an easy way to escape whenever your day needs it.

programme.apres: Keep one world a week as a mini getaway, and explore the ones you haven’t visited yet, like Journey Through the Galaxy or The Heart of the Earth.
